prompts.label: Short answer 1
prompts.prompt: Tell us about an aspect of your life so far or your lived experience that is important to you, and describe how it has shaped the way you would learn from and contribute to Columbia's multidimensional and collaborative environment.

prompts.label: Short answer 2
prompts.prompt: At Columbia, students representing a wide range of perspectives are invited to live and learn together. In such a community, questions and debates naturally arise. Please describe a time when you did not agree with someone and discuss how you engaged with them and what you took away from the interaction.

prompts.label: Short answer 3

prompts.label: Short answer 4

prompts.label: Bridge builders
prompts.prompt: We are looking for students who want to be bridge builders—students who can connect people, groups, and ideas to span divides, foster understanding, and promote collaboration within a dynamic, interconnected, and vibrant global academic community. We are eager for you to tell us how your experiences have helped you understand what qualities and efforts are needed to bridge divides so that people can better learn and work together. Please consider one or more of the following questions in your essay.
options: Tell us about a time you encountered a perspective different from your own. What did you learn—about yourself, the other person, or the world?
Tell us about an experience you’ve had working with others who have different perspectives. What role did you try to play in helping people to work together, and what did you learn from your efforts?

Tell us about someone you’ve observed who does a particularly good job helping people think or work together. How does this person set the stage for common exploration or work? How do they react when challenges arise? What qualities do you admire in this person?

prompts.label: Why this major
prompts.prompt: Why did you choose the major you did?

prompts.label: Honors or community
prompts.prompt: Answer the question that fits you: the first if you're interested in Commonwealth Honors College, the second if not.
options: Commonwealth Honors College is a community in which students examine complex questions, learn across differences, and connect their academic interests to the world around them. What is one perspective, experience, or question you would bring to this community, and how would you hope to develop it at UMass Amherst?

At UMass Amherst, no two students are alike. Our communities and groups often define us and shape our individual worlds. Community can refer to various aspects, including shared geography, religion, race/ethnicity, income, ideology, and more. Please choose one of your communities or groups and describe its significance. Explain how, as a product of this community or group, you would enrich our campus.

prompts.label: Written supplement
prompts.prompt: Answer one of these four prompts. The written supplement is optional: you can send a written response, a video, or both.
options: List five books you’ve read that have intrigued you. (150 character limit per book title)

Tell us what piques your intellectual curiosity or has helped you understand the world’s complexity. This can include a work you’ve read, a project you’ve completed for a class, and even co-curricular activities in which you have been involved. (150 word limit)

Dr. Maya Angelou, renowned author, poet, civil-rights activist, and former Wake Forest University Reynolds Professor of American Studies, inspired others to celebrate their identities and to honor each person’s dignity. Choose one of Dr. Angelou’s powerful quotes. How does this quote relate to your lived experience or reflect how you plan to contribute to the Wake Forest community? (300 word limit)
Give us your Top Ten List. (The choice of theme is yours.) (100 character limit per line)
